```{r}
create_selection_table <- function(all_variables, selected_lists) {
  
  # Initialize the data frame with the variable column
  result_table <- data.frame(Variable = all_variables, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  # Define the exact order of the desired columns
  regions <- c("Norte", "Nordeste", "Sudeste", "Sul", "Centro-Oeste", "Nacional")
  
  # Loop to fill each column
  for (region in regions) {
    # Check if the region was provided in the selected list
    if (region %in% names(selected_lists)) {
      # Mark with 'X' if the variable is in that region's vector, otherwise leave blank
      result_table[[region]] <- ifelse(all_variables %in% selected_lists[[region]], "X", "")
    } else {
      # If any model is missing, fill with blanks to maintain structure
      result_table[[region]] <- ""
    }
  }
  
  return(result_table)
}
```

## Post-LASSO

```{r}
clean_lasso_names <- function(matrix, variables) {
  
  # Create an empty vector
  clean_vector <- c()
  
  # Iterate over variables in the matrix, one hot encoded
  for (matrix_name in matrix) {
    
    # Iterate over the list of original variables
    for (orig_var in variables) {
      
      # If the matrix name starts exactly with the original variable name
      if (startsWith(matrix_name, orig_var)) {
        clean_vector <- c(clean_vector, orig_var)
        break # Exit the inner loop 
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Get unique from multiple categories
  clean_vector <- unique(clean_vector)
  
  return(clean_vector)
}
```

```{r}
clean_select_vars_national <- clean_lasso_names(select_vars_national, relevant_variables)
print(clean_select_vars_national)
```

```{r}
create_formula <- function(y, x) {
  right_side <- paste(x, collapse = " + ")
  equation <- paste(y, "~", right_side)
  formula <- as.formula(equation)
  return(formula)
}
```

```{r}
formula_national <- create_formula(
  y = "tenure_condition",
  x = clean_select_vars_national
)

formula_national
```

```{r}
post_lasso_nationl <- svy_vglm(
  formula = formula_national,
  design = pnadc,
  family = multinomial
)
```

levels(pnadc$variables$tenure_condition)

```{r}
# 1. Extract the raw summary object
mod_sum <- summary(post_lasso_national)

# 2. THE ULTIMATE FIX: Dynamically search for the matrix!
# We ask R to look at the names inside the summary object and pick the right one.
if ("coeftable" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coeftable
} else if ("coefficients" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coefficients
} else if ("coef3" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coef3
} else {
  # Fallback if the object itself is the matrix
  raw_matrix <- as.matrix(mod_sum)
}

# Quick safety check: If it's STILL empty, stop and warn the user
if (is.null(raw_matrix) || nrow(raw_matrix) == 0) {
  stop("Error: The matrix is still empty. Please run `names(summary(modelo_post_lasso_nacional))` in your console and check what names appear.")
}

# 3. Build a fresh data frame manually 
clean_df <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(raw_matrix),
  Estimate_B = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 1]),
  Std_Error = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 2]),
  Wald_z = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 3]),
  Sig = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 4]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 4. Clean the text and calculate the Odds Ratio in Base R
clean_df$Variable <- sub(":.*", "", clean_df$Term)
clean_df$Equation <- sub(".*:", "Category ", clean_df$Term)
clean_df$Exp_B <- exp(clean_df$Estimate_B)

# 5. Order the columns exactly as needed
final_data <- clean_df[, c("Equation", "Variable", "Estimate_B", "Std_Error", "Wald_z", "Sig", "Exp_B")]

# 6. Render the academic table using gt
final_table <- final_data %>%
  group_by(Equation) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    Estimate_B = "Estimate B",
    Std_Error = "Std. error",
    Wald_z = "Wald",
    Sig = "Sig.",
    Exp_B = "Exp(B)"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(Estimate_B, Std_Error, Wald_z, Sig, Exp_B),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Sig, rows = Sig < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**TABLE 4**"),
    subtitle = "Multinomial logit model tenure choice"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    row_group.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.background.color = "#f0f0f0",
    table.border.top.color = "black",
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table_body.hlines.color = "lightgray"
  )

# Display the beautiful table
final_table
```
